headline: NVIDIA Rockets 31.48% as Huang's Return Reignites the AI Trade
body_html:
NVIDIA surged 31.48% on Monday after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, a reversal that followed intervention from President Trump. The S&P 500 jumped roughly 4.5% on the news. NVIDIA's move changed more market value than any other company's by a wide margin and gave the AI trade a fresh jolt.

The buying spread well beyond one name. Of 663 stocks in our universe, 603 rose and 59 fell. Semiconductors led the sectors with an average gain of 12.85%, ahead of Financials at 8.15%, Materials at 4.39% and Industrials at 4.36%. Micron climbed 19.04% and TSMC rose 14.03%, while Astera Labs gained 23.16%. Energy lagged the field, averaging a 1.42% gain.

Weakness was scarce. CrowdStrike fell 8.92%, the session's largest decline, and several oil and gas names slipped. The mood was lopsided, and a day this one-directional leaves the market with a question for Tuesday, November 24: whether the rally can hold now that the headline has been absorbed. Fed official John Williams has said higher rates are likely over time to address inflation.

briefs.headline: TSMC Bounces After a Rough Week
briefs.body: TSMC rose 14.03% as the foundry giant joined the chip rally. The shares had come into the session after a weekly slide of roughly 20%, tied to worries over NVIDIA and fresh US export curbs on China. The company has also paused advanced chip shipments to China.

briefs.headline: Micron Leads the Memory Rebound
briefs.body: Micron gained 19.04%, one of the largest moves among big-cap names. Commentary pointed to Huang's return as the spark for chip stocks. The rally also follows a recent selloff, and the company's president recently criticized rival DRAM designs.

briefs.headline: Connectivity Chips Race Higher
briefs.body: The AI plumbing names ran hard. Astera Labs rose 23.16%, Credo Technology gained 22.63%, MaxLinear advanced 21.38% and Semtech added 18.83%. All four sit among the day's top gainers, a sign that the NVIDIA rebound lifted the supply chain around it.

briefs.headline: Financials Take Second Place in Sector Rotation
briefs.body: Financials rose an average of 8.15%, the second-best showing among the sectors we track and well behind only Semiconductors. Separately, New York Fed president John Williams indicated that higher interest rates are likely over time to address inflation, a reminder that policy remains a live question.

briefs.headline: CrowdStrike Swims Against the Tide
briefs.body: CrowdStrike fell 8.92%, the steepest drop in our universe on a day when 603 stocks rose. Software overall still gained an average of 3.66%, so the cybersecurity company's slide stood apart from its sector.

briefs.headline: Energy Names Trail the Rally
briefs.body: Energy was the weakest sector, with an average gain of 1.42%. Baytex Energy fell 3.80%, Texas Pacific Land dropped 3.40% and Chord Energy lost 3.38%. All three ranked among the day's decliners as money moved toward technology and other cyclical groups.
